statement: For a yes/no outcome whose rarer class is below 20% of rows, random oversampling or SMOTE of the rarer class should be applied by default inside each training fold, because it raises the AUC and corrects the model's tendency to underestimate the rarer class's probability, so the decision threshold can stay at 0.5.
regime: yes/no outcome whose rarer class is below 20% of rows, prediction
claimed_basis: van den Goorbergh et al., JAMIA 2022;29:1525.

statement: The signed paired difference between the interpretable benchmark (a properly specified regression with splines on the same in-fold preprocessing) and the best flexible family, with the flexible pick re-made in every bootstrap resample of the out-of-fold predictions (BBC-CV over the flexible set), estimates what interpretability costs or gains on the strictly proper primary and on calibration (distance of the calibration slope from 1) without the optimism of picking the best flexible family; when its 95% percentile interval spans 0 there is 'no measurable cost on these rows'.
regime: prediction; an interpretable benchmark and >=1 flexible family with out-of-fold predictions; >=10 scored rows
decision: the 'what the interpretable model costs or gains' readout (EXPLORE)
claimed_basis: Rudin 2019 (Nat Mach Intell 1:206): 'It is a myth that there is necessarily a trade-off between accuracy and interpretability'; the prediction review ('Remove the selection optimism of picking the "best flexible" family (BBC-CV over the flexible set)'); Tsamardinos et al. 2018 (selection.py:985-997).

statement: Under Estimate or Describe, relabeling a two-valued covariate or energy column that is not the exposure, the outcome, a declared modifier or the fixed-effects column (coding its two spellings the other way round, with no blank and no third spelling) leaves the exposure's coefficient, its interval and the fitted values exactly unchanged and only flips the sign of that column's own coefficient, so the finding's repair changes no reported number and needs no calibration or post-lock check.
regime: Estimate or Describe purpose; finding whose repair family declares reparameterizes and whose offered options only relabel; every affected column has role covariate or energy and is named by no other answer; any outcome type or model family the primary uses
decision: Triage disposition of an open data finding at the gate (open-noticings sweep)
claimed_basis: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell (Frisch & Waugh 1933; Lovell 1963), named in materiality_calibration.json 'invariance' entry; SURFACING_POLICY §2.6 as amended; WAVE_C6A_PLAN §7 ruling 2 (orchestrator, 2026-10-10)

statement: In a nutrition exposure-outcome analysis, demographic covariates (age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, income/poverty ratio, occupation, marital status) are pre-exposure common causes of the exposure and the outcome and belong in the adjustment set as confounders (the criterion's answers: causes exposure yes, causes outcome yes, after exposure no).
regime: Inference (total effect) with a declared exposure; covariates named as demographics; any study design, including cross-sectional.
decision: Pre-filled answers on the adjustment card (modified disjunctive cause criterion), confirmed in one tap per block.
claimed_basis: NUTRITION_PACK §08 (Models 1 and 2); VanderWeele 2019 Eur J Epidemiol 34:211-219.

statement: The regression-calibration interval is the percentile interval of the bootstrap resamples, 200 by default, and is shown only when at least 90% of the resamples could be calibrated; resamples whose day-to-day error swamped the between-person spread are dropped, which may pull the interval's end away from zero too near.
decision: interval reported or withheld for the calibrated coefficient
claimed_basis: MIN_BOOT_SHARE labeled 'a stated floor'; no source for 200 percentile resamples.

statement: Under complete-case analysis, rows are dropped only for blanks in the predictors the user has confirmed and kept. Blanks in a column whose blanks are coded as their own 'Missing' level are values, not missing data, and drop no row. A role that rode along unconfirmed drops no row, and the fit waits for its confirmation.

Subgroup performance with intervals is reported only for groups of at least 10 rows and, for a yes/no outcome, at least 5 rows of each class; smaller groups are named but not scored; an amount column is grouped into thirds at its 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles and a code column by its levels.
decision: Which subgroups are scored and how a column is grouped

statement: Change-in-estimate selection among covariates already judged pre-exposure causes cannot detect mediators or colliders, and for an odds ratio or hazard ratio with a common outcome the estimate changes from non-collapsibility even without confounding, so it is block-and-record under inference and conflicts with OR/HR estimands for common outcomes.
regime: inference; data-driven adjustment by change-in-estimate; OR or HR with a common outcome for the invalidity part
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 1(c); §2 'an OR or HR with a common outcome conflicts with change-in-estimate'

statement: Internal–external cross-validation across survey cycles is summarized by random-effects meta-analysis of the log MSE with a Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman interval and a prediction interval for a new cycle on t(k − 2), because on the identity scale cycles with larger MSE have larger standard errors and so less weight, which is optimistic.
claimed_basis: Riley et al. 2016; Higgins, Thompson & Spiegelhalter 2009; IntHout et al. 2014; Snell et al. 2018

statement: A prediction model that reads a predictor known only after its intended moment of use looks better in a paper than in use, so only predictors recorded at that moment are read (e.g., no 24-hour recall for a clinic use).
regime: prediction; intended use and moment of use

statement: Under prediction on survey data with weights, ordinary unweighted K-fold cross-validation with folds drawn at random over rows estimates the surveyed population's performance without bias, because randomly drawn folds are themselves simple random samples of the design.
regime: prediction on complex survey data (strata, PSUs, weights), population performance wanted
claimed_basis: MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 13; Wieczorek, Guerin & McMahon, Stat 2022;11:e454.

statement: Sorting or permuting the rows of a table before an ordinary least-squares fit leaves its coefficients, intervals and fitted values unchanged, so the app does not shuffle rows before a least-squares fit.
decision: row order before a least-squares fit
claimed_basis: Invariance of X'X and X'y to row permutation.
